text:
maria: FYI QA hit a case where partners set a header to force fallbacks and argued it's useful for simulating degraded regions. We need a safe rollout + telemetry before we expose anything in the SDK.
ajay: what header are they using? is this the same as the old dev-only flag? we should avoid adding a general-purpose escape hatch.
maria: they called it `x-rw-route-sim` in their tests. example they sent:
```
x-rw-region-hint: eu-west-1
x-rw-tier-override: enterprise
x-rw-route-sim: force-fallback
```
olivia: hmm can we make it token-scoped? only internal tokens / teams can flip that. also console needs a toggle for canary usage so support can't accidentally encourage partners to use it in prod.
kevin: telemetry ask: we need a counter and hist for any request that triggers a simulated fallback. suggested metric names: `routing.sim.force_fallback.count` and `routing.sim.force_fallback.latency_ms` with tags: region,tier,model_variant,client_id.
ajay: agree on telemetry. runtime-wise we should only honor the header when: token has scope `routing:simulate` OR header includes `mode=canary` and request comes from internal IP range.
maria: +1. also make the SDK respect env var RW_ALLOW_ROUTE_SIM for dev builds only. avoid accidentally shipping to prod packages.
infra-monitor: noticed a spike in fallback rate yesterday: `routing.fallback.count{region:us-east-1} +420%` — looks like an internal test leaked. link: https://infra.example/alerts/12345
olivia: Yikes. That supports the token-scope guard. We should also emit an audit event with full request id and user so we can revert and notify customers if needed.
kevin: dashboard: add a panel grouped by `simulate_source` (token|env|internal-ip|sdk) and a rate over time. Add an alert when `routing.sim.force_fallback.count` > 100/min for non-test clients.
ajay: small API contract proposal:
- header name `x-rw-route-sim`
- allowed values: `off`, `simulate:force-fallback`, `simulate:penalize-region`
- only accepted if `Authorization` token scope includes `routing:simulate`
- runtime logs audit event `route_sim` with tags
maria: sounds good. can we also add a dry-run mode that only logs what would have happened (no actual fallback) — `simulate:dry-run`.
ajay: yes `simulate:dry-run` should be default for non-internal tokens.
maria: console UX: add a rollout card under Routing -> Simulations with a big warning, ability to limit by org, client_id, and a canary toggle. Link to support playbook.
olivia: also need quota behavior: simulated fallbacks still consume quota like normal requests, but we should tag them so billing can optionally be excluded for internal tests.
kevin: add metric `routing.sim.billed` boolean tag. and export to billing job for exclusion filter.
ajay: I'll open a PR in the SDK that adds the header handling and env var guard, plus tests for token-scope logic. Maria can follow with runtime + telemetry PR.
maria: cool — I'll create the runtime PR and a Datadog dashboard draft. can someone from security review token scope change? @kevin?
kevin: on it. will do a quick review and flag any RBAC implications.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: routing-sim feature flag -> 5% of internal orgs (id: 983). changelist: infra/route-sim v2 -> 2026-03-20T14:12Z
olivia: thanks. once canary stable let's add a console probe to let SRE toggle sim on/off per org without redeploy.
maria: will follow up with PR links and a short runbook. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
